title: Rami bar Yechezkel
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: Hyman states that in the Babylonian Talmud he is always mentioned as Rami, and in the Jerusalem Talmud as Ami bar Yechezkel.

He was the younger brother of Rav Yehudah, as in [Kiddushin 32a:9-12](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.32a.9-12) and [Sanhedrin 80b:6-8](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.80b.6-8): “Rav Yechezkel taught Rami his son … Rav Yehudah said to him: Father, do not teach it so.”

Hyman suggests that possibly he still received from Rav and Shmuel, as we find in [Chullin 44a](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.44a.6), where he reports a teaching in Rav’s name, and [Ketubot 60a](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.60a.2) and 76a, where he reports teachings in Shmuel’s name. He went up to the Land of Israel, as stated explicitly in [Ketubot 111b](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.111b.22): “Rami bar Yechezkel visited Bnei Brak” (it is known that Bnei Brak is in the Land of Israel, as stated explicitly in Joshua 19:45, a town in the territory of Dan, and the place of Rabbi Akiva’s academy, as in Sanhedrin 32a) “and saw [a land] flowing with milk and honey.” Hyman suggests that apparently he sent from there to Rav Huna: “Tell us some of those fine things that you told us in Rav’s name,” as in [Shabbat 138b:5-6](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.138b.5-6).
Likewise he sent to Rav Amram: “Let the Master tell us some of those fine things that you told us in Rav Assi’s name,” as in [Eruvin 102a](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.102a.13).

Afterward he returned to Babylonia, as in [Ketubot 21a:15](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.21a.15), [Ketubot 60a:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.60a.2) and [Ketubot 76b:9](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.76b.9), where they said: “When Rami bar Yechezkel came, he said: Do not listen to these general rules that Yehudah my brother formulated in Shmuel’s name.”

He brought from there many baraitot, as in [Shabbat 65a:2-3](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.65a.2-3): “Rami bar Yechezkel taught: provided it is tied to her ear … provided it is tied to her sandal.” There, [Shabbat 138a:11](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.138a.11): “One may not make a folded cloak.”

In [Eruvin 14b:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.14b.5): “The sea that Solomon made — its lower three cubits were square.” There, [Eruvin 58b:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.58b.6), he is quoted on measuring a slope. In [Sukkah 26a:15](https://www.sefaria.org/Sukkah.26a.15): “How long is a casual sleep? The time to walk a hundred cubits.” In [Yevamot 12a:11](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.12a.11): “If she refused the husband, she is permitted to his father.” There, [Yevamot 16a:15-16](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.16a.15-16): “Converts are not accepted from the Kartuyim.” In [Bava Kamma 18b:17](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.18b.17): “A rooster that stuck its head into the air of a glass vessel and broke it pays full damage.” In [Sanhedrin 15b:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.15b.6): “Just as a man’s death is by twenty-three, so too an animal.”

All of them are baraitot; Hyman finds only one place where he stated a halakhah of his own, in [Bava Batra 160b:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.160b.6), where he brings proof from a verse that a plain document has two witnesses and a tied one three.

And what he said in [Yoma 58b:11-13](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.58b.11-13), “The sea that Solomon made … every turn that you turn should be only to the right,” is a baraita, as cited in [Zevachim 62b:8](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.62b.8), except that there it reads Rami bar Chizkiyah; Hyman proposes Yechezkel.
He is mentioned in Jerusalem Talmud Eruvin 6:1, folio 27a: “Rabbi Ba, citing Ami bar Yechezkel in Rav’s name.”
In [Jerusalem Talmud Taanit 2:14:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Taanit.2.14.3): “Rabbi Ba said in the name of Rabbi Imi bar Yechezkel, who reported in the name of Rav.”[^3][^4]

notes.text: The source says he saw flowing milk and honey; no claim that goats produced honey. Always Rami versus Palestinian Ami is Hyman’s stated spelling observation. The reciter role, younger-brother relation, all kinships, baraitot and proposed Chizkiyah-to-Yechezkel correction remain separate, with no global name harmonization.

The consulted Ketubot 111b has milk dripping from goats and honey from figs, not goats producing honey. The current body’s abbreviated flowing milk and honey is retained. Hyman’s always Rami/Ami observation, younger-brother relation, travel chronology, baraita classification, one-own-halakhah claim and Chizkiyah/Yechezkel proposal remain separate attributed observations.

Ketubot describes milk dripping from goats and honey from figs. Chullin and Ketubot show Rami correcting his brother’s reports from Rav and Shmuel. In Eruvin he asks Rav Amram for a report in Rav Asi’s name.

The list that places Rabbi Akiva at Bnei Brak appears at [Sanhedrin 32b:10](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.32b.10) (Hyman cites 32a). [Ketubot 76b:9](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.76b.9) gives Rami’s correction of Yehudah’s report from Shmuel (Hyman also cites 76a). The consulted [Jerusalem Talmud Eruvin 5:1:12](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Eruvin.5.1.12) has Rabbi Ba and Ami bar Yechezkel in Rav’s name (Hyman cites 6:1, folio 27a). The Hebrew of [Jerusalem Talmud Taanit 2:14:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Taanit.2.14.3) explicitly gives Rabbi Ba in Rabbi Imi’s name, in Rav’s name. [Seder HaDorot 592](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=592&lang=en) directs readers from Ami bar Yechezkel to Rami bar Yechezkel.
